category_title: Middle school students with IDD who independently navigate UDL literacy environments using audio supports and social features
student_description: These are middle school students with IDD who are highly motivated by autonomy, social interaction, and age-appropriate content. They can independently navigate digital platforms and use embedded supports (like audio) to access complex texts, but they struggle with spelling/mechanics and become easily discouraged by a lack of peer social feedback. They uniquely need targeted, non-intrusive writing support, compensatory teacher praise, and absolute respect for their content choices.

criteria.rationale: Explicit upfront training on the digital environment ensures the student can independently access embedded supports like audio reading and sentence starters.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must include a phase dedicated to explicitly teaching the student how to navigate the platform and use its embedded tools.

criteria.rationale: While the student needs initial 1-on-1 help, their ultimate goal and capability is complete independence in navigating the platform and choosing tasks.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must explicitly describe a progression from high initial one-on-one support to diminished support and independent work.
